title: Jersey · the five-kick bounce
text: Play Kick L with your left hand. Count 1 e & a, 2 e & a, 3 e & a, 4 e & a. Kicks land on 1, 2, 3, 3 a and 4 &.

intro.goal: Keep the five-kick shape even across the loop.
intro.watch: The final three kicks form a 3–3–2 grouping of sixteenth notes. These are dotted-eighth gaps, not evenly spaced triplets.

title: Jersey · backbeat bounce
text: Kick L and Clap are both left-hand pads and coincide on beat 2. Prepare both pads before the simultaneous hit.

intro.goal: Keep the kick shape while adding two claps.
intro.watch: The clap on 4 sits between the last two kicks. Keep it independent; do not move either kick to the clap.

title: Jersey · right-hand anchor
text: Keep the same left-hand pattern. Add Hat R with your right hand on beats 2 and 4. Listen to each layer before playing all three.

intro.goal: Land the simultaneous kick, clap and hat together.
intro.watch: Beat 2 has three pads at once, with two played by the left hand. Keep the wrist loose and avoid a flam.

title: Jersey · a snare answer
text: Your left hand plays kick; it plays Snare L on 3 and 3 a. Your right hand keeps hats on 2 and 4. This exercise changes the previous clap layer to a snare layer.

intro.goal: Place the snare with the last part of the bounce.
intro.watch: Kick and snare coincide twice. Both pads must land together, without rushing toward the final kick.

title: Jersey · two-bar snare twist
text: Bar 1 is the previous groove. In bar 2 add a quieter left-hand snare on 3 & before the snare on 3 a. Your right hand keeps hats on 2 and 4.

intro.goal: Keep the kick unchanged through a quieter extra snare.
intro.watch: The extra snare is a softer note, not an extra kick. Count both bars and keep the five-kick shape unchanged.

title: Jersey · groove and break
text: Your left hand keeps the Jersey kick and plays clap on 2 and 4. Your right hand plays eighth-note hats, then rests on the final 4 & of bar 2. Return together on bar 1.

intro.goal: Hold eighth-note hats and return cleanly after their break.
intro.watch: Keep the missing final hat silent while playing the final kick. This is an original performance variation, not a transcription of a record.

title: Footwork · half-time pulse
text: Your right hand keeps hats on 1, 2, 3 and 4. Your left hand plays kick on 1 and 3 and adds Snare L on 3. The slower starting tempo is for learning.

intro.goal: Keep a calm quarter-note pulse beneath a half-time snare.
intro.watch: Beat 3 joins three pads. Count all four beats even when the snare gives the groove a slower feel.

title: Footwork · displaced kicks
text: Your right hand keeps quarter-note hats. Your left hand plays kick on 1, 2 &, 3 & and 4 & and places the snare on 3. This is an original syncopation study.

intro.goal: Place syncopated kicks between the right-hand pulse.
intro.watch: The offbeat kicks must stay between hats. Avoid dragging the snare forward to meet the following kick.

title: Footwork · snare burst
text: Keep the kick and right-hand hats. Your left hand plays snare on 3, then 3 a and 4. Start slowly: the last two snare hits are one sixteenth note apart.

intro.goal: Play a short snare burst without changing the pulse.
intro.watch: The snare on 4 must join the right-hand hat. Use small taps; the burst must not pull the next bar early.

title: Footwork · triplet feel
text: This lesson has 12 steps per bar: three equal parts per beat. Your right hand keeps hats on each beat. Your left hand plays kick on 1, the second triplet of 2, 3, and the third triplet of 3 and adds snare on 3.

intro.goal: Place triplet-grid kicks around the steady beat.
intro.watch: These subdivisions are actual equal triplets. They differ from the Jersey 3–3–2 grouping. Listen first and count three equal parts per beat.

title: Footwork · hat response
text: Your right hand keeps quarter-note closed hats and adds Open hat on 2 & and 4 &, with left-hand kick. Your left hand keeps snare on 3. The next closed hat cuts the open sound.

intro.goal: Answer the pulse with open hats and close them on the next beat.
intro.watch: Return your right hand to the closed hat without rushing. Check the open-hat pad before starting; it sits above the closed-hat pad.

title: Footwork · two-bar talk
text: Bar 1 uses the displaced-kick study. Bar 2 adds two close final kicks on 4 e and 4 &, and an answering snare on 4. Your right hand keeps quarter-note hats throughout.

intro.goal: Join two different kick phrases while keeping the right hand steady.
intro.watch: Keep the second bar the same length as the first. The two final kicks are only one sixteenth apart. This is an original footwork-inspired study.
